name: Mark

overview.author: John Mark, companion of Paul and Barnabas and later of Peter, whose preaching early tradition says Mark recorded (Acts 12:12; 1 Peter 5:13).
overview.date: Probably the mid-50s to late 60s AD, likely from Rome.
overview.audience: Primarily Gentile Christians, likely in Rome, facing persecution. Mark explains Jewish customs and translates Aramaic words.
overview.setting: Jesus’ ministry in Galilee and His final week in Jerusalem.
overview.purpose: To present Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God, who acts with authority and came to serve and suffer, and to call disciples to follow Him on the way of the cross.
overview.structure: A fast-moving narrative (“immediately” appears often). Jesus’ Galilean ministry (1–8:26), the turning point at Peter’s confession and the journey to Jerusalem (8:27–10:52), and the passion week and resurrection (11–16).

themes.title: Jesus the Son of God
themes.text: Mark begins and climaxes (15:39) with this confession.

themes.title: Authority
themes.text: Jesus has authority over demons, disease, nature, sin, and the Sabbath.

themes.title: The Suffering Servant
themes.text: “The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve” (10:45).

themes.title: The Messianic Secret
themes.text: Jesus often tells people not to reveal Him until the cross reveals who He is.

themes.title: Discipleship and Failure
themes.text: The disciples misunderstand repeatedly, yet Jesus keeps calling them.

themes.title: Faith and Fear
themes.text: Jesus calls people from fear to faith.

themes.title: Urgency
themes.text: The kingdom has arrived, and Mark’s narrative moves “immediately.”

christInBook.text: The gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
Jesus gives His life as a ransom for many, fulfilling Isaiah 53.
Jesus claims to be the Christ and the Son of Man of Daniel 7.
The torn curtain and the centurion’s confession reveal Jesus at His death.
“He has risen; he is not here.”

reflection: Mark’s Jesus is constantly on the move to serve. What would it look like to serve rather than be served this week?
Where do you relate to “I believe; help my unbelief”?
How do the disciples’ failures encourage you?
What does taking up your cross mean in your current season?
How does Mark 10:45 change how you see your own worth and purpose?

chapterList.title: The Beginning of the Gospel
chapterList.summary: “The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.” John baptizes; Jesus is baptized and hears the Father’s voice. He is tempted in the wilderness, preaches the kingdom, calls fishermen, casts out an unclean spirit, heals Peter’s mother-in-law and many others, prays in a desolate place, and cleanses a leper.
questions: What does Mark’s first verse tell you about his purpose?
What does it mean to “repent and believe in the gospel” (1:15)?
What does Jesus’ early morning prayer (1:35) teach?

chapterList.title: Authority to Forgive
chapterList.summary: Four friends lower a paralytic through a roof; Jesus forgives and heals him. He calls Levi and eats with sinners: “I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.” He teaches about new wine in new wineskins and declares that the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.
questions: What do the four friends teach about bringing others to Jesus?
Why did forgiving sins offend the scribes?
How does Jesus see the Sabbath (2:27–28)?

chapterList.title: The Twelve and Jesus’ True Family
chapterList.summary: Jesus heals a withered hand on the Sabbath, and the Pharisees plot with the Herodians. He appoints the twelve “so that they might be with him” and be sent out. His family thinks He is out of His mind, and scribes accuse Him of Beelzebul. “Whoever does the will of God, he is my brother and sister and mother.”
questions: Why did Jesus first call the twelve “to be with him” (3:14)?
What is Jesus’ answer to the Beelzebul charge?
Who belongs to Jesus’ family (3:35)?

chapterList.title: Parables and the Storm
chapterList.summary: Jesus teaches the parable of the sower, the lamp, the growing seed, and the mustard seed. That evening He calms a great storm: “Why are you so afraid? Have you still no faith?” The disciples ask, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
questions: What hinders the word from bearing fruit in your life?
What does the growing seed teach about God’s work (4:26–29)?
How does Jesus address the disciples’ fear?

chapterList.title: Power Over Demons, Disease, and Death
chapterList.summary: Jesus frees a man possessed by a legion of demons, who then tells what Jesus did for him. A woman with a 12-year bleeding touches His garment and is healed: “Your faith has made you well.” Jesus raises Jairus’s daughter: “Talitha cumi.”
questions: How did the healed man respond, and how did the townspeople?
Why did Jesus stop to find the woman who touched Him?
How does “Do not fear, only believe” (5:36) speak to you?

chapterList.title: Rejected and Sent
chapterList.summary: Jesus is rejected in Nazareth. He sends out the twelve. Herod beheads John. Jesus has compassion on the crowd and feeds five thousand. He walks on the sea, telling the frightened disciples, “Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid.” He heals many in Gennesaret.
questions: Why did familiarity breed unbelief in Nazareth?
What moved Jesus to feed the crowd (6:34)?
Why were the disciples’ hearts hardened (6:52)?

chapterList.title: What Defiles
chapterList.summary: The Pharisees criticize unwashed hands. Jesus says they abandon God’s commandment for tradition, and that what comes out of the heart defiles. A Syrophoenician woman’s faith wins her daughter’s healing. Jesus heals a deaf man: “Ephphatha,” “Be opened.”
questions: How do human traditions replace God’s word today?
What evils come from the heart (7:21–23)?
What does the woman’s response (7:28) show?

chapterList.title: Who Do You Say I Am?
chapterList.summary: Jesus feeds four thousand. The disciples still do not understand. Jesus heals a blind man in two stages. Peter confesses, “You are the Christ.” Jesus teaches that the Son of Man must suffer, die, and rise, rebukes Peter, and calls disciples to take up their cross.
questions: What does the two-stage healing picture about the disciples’ understanding?
Why did Peter reject Jesus’ prediction?
What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and lose his soul?

chapterList.title: Transfiguration and Greatness
chapterList.summary: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John. He heals a boy whose father cries, “I believe; help my unbelief!” He again predicts His death. The disciples argue about who is greatest; Jesus says, “If anyone would be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.”
questions: How does the transfiguration prepare the disciples for the cross?
What does the father’s prayer (9:24) teach about faith?
How does Jesus redefine greatness (9:35–37)?

chapterList.title: The Servant Who Gives His Life
chapterList.summary: Jesus teaches on marriage, blesses children, and loves a rich man who goes away sad. He predicts His death a third time. James and John ask for glory; Jesus says He came “to give his life as a ransom for many.” Blind Bartimaeus cries for mercy, is healed, and follows Jesus on the way.
questions: Why did Jesus look at the rich man and love him (10:21)?
How does 10:45 explain the purpose of Jesus’ life?
How does Bartimaeus model discipleship?

chapterList.title: The King Enters Jerusalem
chapterList.summary: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a colt as crowds shout “Hosanna!” He curses a fig tree and drives out the money changers: “My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations.” He teaches about faith and forgiveness in prayer. The leaders question His authority.
questions: What does the fruitless fig tree represent?
Why did Jesus say “for all the nations” (11:17)?
How are prayer and forgiveness linked (11:25)?

chapterList.title: Controversies and the Widow’s Offering
chapterList.summary: Jesus tells the parable of the wicked tenants. He answers questions on taxes, resurrection, and the greatest commandment. He warns against the scribes and praises a poor widow who gave two small coins, “everything she had.”
questions: What does the parable of the tenants reveal about Jesus’ identity?
Why did the widow’s gift count more than others’ gifts?
How do you love God with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength?

chapterList.title: Stay Awake
chapterList.summary: Jesus predicts the temple’s destruction and warns of deception, wars, and persecution. The gospel must be proclaimed to all nations. The Son of Man will come in clouds. No one knows the day or hour. “What I say to you I say to all: Stay awake.”
questions: Why does Jesus warn so strongly about deception?
How should the Spirit’s help in persecution encourage you (13:11)?
What does it mean to “stay awake”?

chapterList.title: Anointing, Supper, and Arrest
chapterList.summary: A woman anoints Jesus with costly ointment, and He defends her “beautiful thing.” Jesus shares the Passover and institutes the Lord’s Supper. In Gethsemane He prays, “Abba, Father... remove this cup... Yet not what I will, but what you will.” He is betrayed and arrested, and Peter denies Him. Before the council, Jesus says, “I am.”
questions: What made the woman’s act “beautiful” (14:6)?
What does Gethsemane reveal about Jesus’ humanity and obedience?
How do Jesus’ words “I am” (14:62) declare His identity?

chapterList.title: The Crucifixion
chapterList.summary: Pilate releases Barabbas and hands Jesus over to be crucified. Soldiers mock Him as king. Simon of Cyrene carries His cross. Darkness falls; Jesus cries, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” The temple curtain tears, and the centurion says, “Truly this man was the Son of God!” Joseph of Arimathea buries Him.
questions: Why is the Barabbas exchange so meaningful?
Why is a Gentile centurion the one who confesses Jesus (15:39)?
What does Joseph of Arimathea’s courage teach (15:43)?

chapterList.title: He Has Risen
chapterList.summary: On the first day of the week, women come to anoint Jesus’ body and find the stone rolled away. A young man in white says, “He has risen; he is not here... go, tell his disciples and Peter.” The women flee in fear. (Verses 9–20, not in the earliest manuscripts, record appearances and the commission.)
questions: Why might the angel specifically mention Peter (16:7)?
How do the women respond, and why?
How does the resurrection change everything?

tagline: Jesus the Servant Son of God who came to give His life
readingPlan: 16 chapters: one chapter a day takes 16 days; two a day takes about 8 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
